name: Family Weekend Dinner
description: Come to the Vista House for a fun and casual dinner! Bring your family or come alone! Please RSVP at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeHH0uWC4LGsQhyx9eQtUWWjQBv2FO7wXnsF_drOIMeGvaTgQ/viewform

name: The Art of Play: Intersections Among Creativity & Spirituality: A MCF Forum led by Dr. David Bernardy
description: We invite you to join us for an interactive forum opportunity with Dr. David Bernardy from the English Department. Dr. Bernardy will invite us into a discussion about the intersections of art, creativity, and spirituality, as well as provide space and opportunity for some creative (and perhaps Godly) play! We hope you will make plans to join us!

name: Mere Lunch
description: Mere Lunch is an opportunity to gather with peers to discuss a book that has spiritual and social implications for our lives. (in the past we've also read various articles and passages of Scripture.) This semester we will meet to discuss Shane Claiborne's Irresistible Revolution. Our first meeting will be a chance for folks to meet each other, pick up books if they need one, and see a reading schedule for the semester. If you'd like for us to order you a copy of the book, let Amy know. Or add a comment to the RSVP page. The cost will be $10. We hope you'll consider joining us for these lively lunch discussions!

name: $ Four Dollar Dinner
description: Mere Christianity Forum regulars bring slightly eccentric kitchen concoctions to the table weekly. For food that hits somewhere between gourmet soul and glorified comfort. Drop in Sundays @ 6:30pm. Each week a different student or group of students prepares a meal for approximately 35-40 $4 Dinner Attendars. Generally the meals are made with organic food and are delightfully unique. You are guaranteed a new culinary experience every Sunday night. Dinner is served buffet style and people scatter throughout the house and the grounds to enjoy their meal and good company. It is a time when students can enjoy a homecooked meal and get a break from campus life. If you are interested in sharing your culinary talents by cooking a $4 dinner, please contact Amy Canosa or Drew Woten!

name: MCF/Vista House Movie Night + Bonfire
description: Join us at the Vista House once again for an evening of fun and frivolity. We'll have popcorn and other movie-goer favorites and will show The Hunger Games outside at the house. Feel free to bring a blanket or chair! (We'll also have a few to share!) If it rains, we'll just take the party in-doors! After the movie, we'll head down to our fire pit for a good old- fashioned bon-fire complete with S'more making necessities! For directions to the house, click the link! If you need a ride to the house that evening, email Drew Woten!
location: Vista House, off the Swamp Rabbit Trail

name: "Evening With" Dinner Series hosts Rev. Beth Templeton
description: Rev. Beth Templeton is the director of "Their Eyes Were Opened," the poverty education program of United Ministries, a Greenville-based social service agency aimed at eradicating poverty in Greenville county. Rev. Templeton has spent the past 30 years working for poverty alleviation in Greenville and is the author of "Loving Our Neighbor: A Thoughtful Approach to Helping People in Poverty". Join us as we learn about her vocational journey, life, and work in Greenville. The Vista House hosts Furman faculty or local community members as featured guest in Vista House’s ongoing interview series known as “An Evening with…” This allows a small group of Furman students to engage in frank conversation and sharp dialogue with interesting and interested members of the larger Furman community. Please join us for dinner this week! If you would like to attend this Wednesday 7 pm dinner, please RSVP to amy.canosa@furman.edu.
